cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: a standard SLES chassis buffered by a betaine. There is no second anionic surfactant, no reset route and no deep-cleansing claim, so rule C1 applies directly.
cleansingStrength.notes: Laureth-4 (#9) is a nonionic solubilizer, not an extra cleansing route. Lauryl Lactate (#4) is an emollient/refatting ester that slightly softens the cleanse.
counterSignals: SLES is the primary surfactant (#2) and buffering is limited to one amphoteric. This is not a mild amino-acid or nonionic chassis, so 'low' is ruled out.

conditioningLevel.rationale: Moderate: one meaningful conditioning system (cationic guar #5) plus light supporting routes (emollient ester #4, pearlizer #6, late glycerin #17). There is no silicone, so slip stays limited.
counterSignals: Silicone-free ('ohne Silikone'). Glycol Distearate is mainly an opacifier. Glycerin is late (#17). Guar is the only substantive deposition route, which pulls toward 'low'.

weightPotential.rationale: Low: the only deposition route is one cationic guar without a silicone or oil payload for it to carry, plus a light rinse-off ester and a pearlizer, all in an effective SLES/betaine base. The 'one light polymer, weak refatter' low anchor fits.
weightPotential.whyThisBand: W1 sets silicone + cationic guar + late amodimethicone in a sulfate/betaine base at 'moderate'. This formula has neither silicone, only the guar, so it sits one step lower.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: For 'moderate', guar at #5 together with Lauryl Lactate #4 and Glycol Distearate #6 would have to count as 'interacting lighter routes', and guar can build up with repeated use. Not chosen because none of these is a persistent payload and the SLES base gives moderate reset.
counterSignals: Guar is fairly early (#5, before Parfum). Cationic guar can build up on porous or bleached hair with repeated use.
weightPotential.disagreementWithPriorLabel: The batch-04 v1.4 adjudication (2026-09-02) recorded weight 'moderate'. This v1.6 pass says 'low'. Flagged for adjudication. The value decides the fine-hair fit (T1/T4).

customerFit.customer: Viola: wavy, fine strands, high density, medium length, colored and bleached, elastic test 'snaps', dry scalp with no current flakes or itch, main problem dry lengths; also frizz, tangling, low shine, lost wave shape. Uses this shampoo about 1x/week of ~2 washes/week, then Syoss Intense Glaze lamination mask, Neqi leave-in mist, Neqi Opulent Oil.
customerFit.verdictShort: OK to keep as her once-a-week wash if her scalp feels comfortable with it, but it does nothing for her main problem (dry, very fragile lengths). Swap it if her lengths feel rough or tangled after it, or her scalp feels tight.
why: What it is built for: soothing an itchy, sensitive scalp. Viola currently has no itch and no flakes, so she isn't using its main job.

Cleansing: a normal SLES-based cleanse, buffered, not harsh but not especially gentle either. Her bleached hair snaps when stretched, so it is very fragile and porous; a milder cleanse would be kinder to her lengths. At only 1x/week, followed by a rich mask, the extra stress is limited.
Weight: light, no silicones, no oils. That suits fine strands and helps waves keep their shape. Once a week it can also clear residue from the lamination mask and the oil, which may help her waves.
Care: only moderate softness (one conditioning polymer, no silicone). It won't detangle or smooth much on its own, so tangling and frizz right after washing depend on the mask.
Scalp comfort: it contains fragrance and menthol (the cooling feel). Most people are fine with this, but on a dry scalp the cooling can feel tight or tingly. If so, that's a reason to swap.

Engine view: under the v1.6 proposal it would be a normal-scalp shampoo that fits fine and normal strands. Viola's scalp is dry, and this is not a dry-scalp product. The proposal is still blocked for review.
watch: How her lengths feel straight after washing with it compared with her other shampoo: rougher, more tangles, more frizz?
Scalp after washing: tight, tingly, itchy or flaky? (cosmetic comfort only)
Technique: shampoo on the scalp only, let the lather run through the lengths, no scrubbing of the lengths, always follow with the mask.
Lost wave shape is more likely from damage and heavy layering (lamination mask + oil on fine hair) than from this light shampoo.
callQuestions: Which shampoo do you use for your other wash each week, and why did you pick the Totes Meer one - did you have an itchy scalp at some point?
How do your scalp and lengths feel right after this shampoo compared with the other one? Tight or tingly scalp? Rougher or more tangled lengths?
Do you put it only on your scalp or through your lengths too, and how much of the mask and oil do you use? Do your waves look flatter on the days after the oil?
customerFit.boundaries: Cosmetic guidance only. No medical claims. If an itchy or flaky scalp comes back or persists, suggest seeing a doctor or dermatologist rather than treating it with shampoo choice.
